title: The Last Baton: A Golden-Hour 100m Sprint with MeshAsset Props
teaches: Model hero props (baton, finish arch, banner) purely from MeshAsset catmull-clark cages: swept 8-vertex rings, ngon end caps and pinned vertices that keep tips and column joints crisp under subdivision.
Bind a prop to a running skeleton with Attachment/Socket: the baton snaps to hand_r and inherits every stride without a second ApplyAction.

Swap locomotion books by ActionLibrary reference, including a converted Mixamo slow-run clip: the sprint owns the race and the last second past the tape, then a 0.4s blend lands on the jog for the coast-down. Both clips run at their authored root speeds (18.3 and 9.5 km/h) so the feet plant without sliding.
Keep foot IK and grounding exact while driving world travel with deterministic in-place locomotion plus position keyframes.

Cut four cameras (POV, infield photographer pan, POV, finish front) with discrete activeCamera keys, and hide the runner's own head/upper chest with camera-local hiddenBones for a clean first-person sprint.
Grade a golden-hour stadium with ACES at 5200K, warm exponential haze, emissive floodlight panels and seeded confetti volume repeats.
